sections.description:
E
EXPORT CREDITS GUARANTEE SCHEME
(ABOLITION) ORDER, 2001
[Gazette of Pakistan, Extraordinary, Part II,
28th April, 2001]
S.R.O. 249(I)/2001, dated 26-4-2001.--Whereas it is expedient to provide for Abolition of Export Credits
Guarantee Scheme and for matters ancillary thereto;
Now, therefore, in exercise of the powers conferred by section 6 of the
Pakistan Insurance Corporation (Re-organization) Ordinance, 2000 (XXXVI of
2000) read with section 3 thereof, the Federal Government is pleased to make
the following order, namely:--
1. Short title and commencement. ---This Order may be called the Export Credits Guarantee Scheme
(Abolition) Order, 2001.
(2) It shall come into force at once.
2. Abolition of Export Credits Guarantee Scheme.--(1) The Export Credits Guarantee Scheme is
hereby abolished.
(2) On the commencement of this Order,---
(a) the balance funds available with the
Managing Company shall stand transferred to the Finance Division, Government of
Pakistan by depositing the same with the State Bank of Pakistan for credit to
Federal Government account, title and account number of which shall be
intimated to the Managing Company by Ministry of Commerce;
(b) investment held in the name of Export
Credits Guarantee Scheme in--
(i) Defence Saving Certificate;
(ii) Regular Income Certificate of National
Savings;
(iii) N.I.T. Units;
(iv) C.O.I's. of Bankers Equity Limited; and
(v) Short Term deposit with NBP, shall stand
transferred to the Federal Government;
(c) all ECGS offices and entire staff working
at ECGS Wing of the Managing Company any where shall stand transferred to the
Managing Company with immediate effect to be placed by the Establishment
Department of the Managing Company;
(d) the Managing Company shall get all the
accounts maintained by them in ECGS Wing to be audited as on 31st December,
2000;
(e) the Federal Government through the Finance
Division or any other institution or organization to whom the ECGS may
ultimately be transferred or ordered to be managed shall settle all premium
deposits of the exporters held by the Managing Company and also settle the dues
of PIC? Exporters payable by the ECGS;
(f) all cases and litigation in any Court
including of the High Court, shall be handled by the Finance Division or, any
institution or organization to whom the Federal Government through the Finance
Department may entrust all or any of the affairs of the scheme; and
(g) all further, office equipment, vehicles or
any other property relating to the ECGS shall be placed at the disposal of the
Ministry of Finance and the Ministry of Finance may dispose of the same on
their own in accordance with the law and the equitable manner.
3. Repeal.--(1) The
Export Credits Scheme Rules, 1962, are hereby repealed.
(2) Notwithstanding the repeal of the Rules specified in sub?paragraph
(1) anything done, action taken, power exercised, decision made under the said
Rules, immediately before the commencement of this order, shall be deemed to
have been validly done, taken, exercised and made and shall have had effect
accordingly.
